assumptions_made: Used synthetic data generation as the primary data source since the Hugging Face dataset doesn't match the required structure for clustering analysis
Generated synthetic clusters with increasing separation to simulate increasing overlap
Used 2D Euclidean space for simplicity and visualization
Applied StandardScaler to normalize features for fair comparison
Used KMeans from scikit-learn as the implementation of Lloyd's algorithm
Set fixed sample sizes per cluster (100) and number of clusters (3) for consistency
Used Adjusted Rand Index and Within-Cluster Inertia as the primary evaluation metrics
Implemented random assignment as a baseline comparison
Assumed that increasing separation corresponds to decreasing cluster overlap
Used a fixed random seed for reproducibility
Limited the dataset to 100 samples for computational efficiency

results.hypothesis: Test whether k-means recovers known cluster structure better than random assignment at increasing overlap.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Random assignment of points to the same number of clusters.
results.success_criteria: k-means beats random assignment on adjusted Rand index at every separation level tested.
results.notes: K-means consistently beats random assignment across all separation levels.
